paper_title: Thermal aware task assignment for multicore processors using genetic algorithm

scenario.description: Quad-Core O3 (out-of-order) processor with simulation of 20 benchmark tasks from Spec2006, MiBench, and MediaBench suites executed over 10 hyper-periods. Two simulation cases: (1) equal initial core temperatures at 45°C, and (2) different initial temperatures (65.48°C, 49.77°C, 45.82°C, 51.86°C).
scenario.architecture: Quad-Core O3 out-of-order processor with 32KB I-Cache and D-Cache per core, dedicated 1MB L2-Cache per core, 64MB RAM with DDRx1 memory controller, 2 GHz clock frequency
scenario.workload: 20 mixed benchmarks: 5 from Spec2006 (bzip2, hmmer, lbm, mcf, sjeng), 6 from MiBench (basicmath, bitcount, qsort, susan, patricia, sha, blowfish, pgp, tiff2bw, typeset), and 9 from MediaBench (FFT/IFFT, PEGWIT, EPIC, RASTA, Ghostscript) with execution times ranging from 62.553 ms to 882.386 ms and energy from 62.0162 mJ to 796.325 mJ
scenario.operating_point: Ambient temperature 45°C, genetic algorithm task assignment with energy-weighted load balancing across cores using decision factors derived from thermal RC-model with unspecified R and C parameters

original_setup.optimizer: Genetic algorithm with tournament selection, single-point crossover, bitwise mutation
original_setup.controller: Task assignment algorithm (Algorithm-1) using energy-weighted load balancing with decision factors derived from core temperatures
original_setup.benchmark: Mixed workload: 5 Spec2006 (bzip2, hmmer, lbm, mcf, sjeng), 6 MiBench (basicmath, bitcount, qsort, susan, patricia, sha, blowfish, pgp, tiff2bw, typeset), 9 MediaBench (FFT/IFFT, PEGWIT, EPIC, RASTA, Ghostscript) tasks executed over 10 hyper-periods

thermal_observable.aggregation: peak difference across all cores per hyper-period

physical_mismatches.reason: Thermal RC parameters (R and C) not specified in paper; equations (1) and (2) use uncharacterized thermal resistance and capacitance values
No 3D chip geometry provided; simulation uses abstract task-to-core mapping without spatial heat distribution
Genetic algorithm parameters (population size Np, iterations iter, tournament size k, crossover probability ρc, mutation probability ρm) not quantified in text or tables
Initial temperature boundary conditions differ between Case 1 (equal 45°C) and Case 2 (65.48°C, 49.77°C, 45.82°C, 51.86°C) but ambient temperature fixed at 45°C; cooling model not described
HotSpot simulator invoked but configuration parameters (floorplan, model file, solver settings) not provided or referenced
GEM5 and McPAT simulators used to derive task power and execution time but exact configuration, command-line options, and output files not documented

studio_assumptions: Task power consumption and execution time are deterministic and obtained from GEM5 and McPAT simulators without validation against real hardware
Energy of each task is simply the product of power and execution time (Eni = Pi * ti) with no consideration of power transients or mode-switching overhead
Thermal RC-model with fixed unspecified parameters accurately represents transient temperature response of all four cores identically
Task assignment algorithm guarantees energy balance within genetic algorithm fitness function but does not account for task migration overhead or scheduling latency
HotSpot simulator output converges to steady-state within each hyper-period such that final core temperatures become initial conditions for the next period
Cores are thermally decoupled except through the RC-model equations; no lateral heat spreading or coupling between adjacent cores modeled
All 20 benchmark tasks are independent, non-preemptive, periodic, and can be arbitrarily assigned to any core without dependency violations or cache effects
Genetic algorithm converges to near-optimal task allocation within fixed iteration count; no proof of convergence or optimality provided
Ambient temperature remains constant at 45°C throughout simulation; no transient cooling effects or air-flow dynamics considered
Task execution times measured in GEM5 are invariant with respect to core temperature, power state, and memory subsystem contention
missing_inputs: Thermal RC-model parameters: thermal resistance R (K/W) and thermal capacitance C (J/K) values for the quad-core processor
HotSpot simulator version, floorplan file (.flp), thermal model file (.model), and solver configuration parameters (transient or steady-state, time step, convergence tolerance)
GEM5 simulator configuration: full command-line options, gem5 version, CPU model details, memory hierarchy parameters, and output statistics files
McPAT simulator configuration: version, XML architecture definition file, and power model parameters used to extract task power consumption
Genetic algorithm hyperparameters: population size Np, number of iterations iter, tournament size k, crossover probability ρc, mutation probability ρm, and elitism strategy
Task benchmark details: exact SPEC CPU2006, MiBench, and MediaBench suite versions; compiler flags; input dataset sizes; and reproducibility information
Validation against real hardware: no comparison with actual quad-core processor measurements or independent thermal sensor data
Code availability: no repository URL, supplementary code, or simulation scripts provided for Algorithm-1, genetic algorithm implementation, or integration with GEM5/McPAT/HotSpot
Complete floorplan geometry: die size, core dimensions, L2-cache location, memory controller placement relative to cores, and thermal interface material (TIM) properties
Uncertainty quantification: no error bars, confidence intervals, or sensitivity analysis for thermal RC-model, genetic algorithm convergence, or benchmark repeatability
